description: ZALF published 173 soil hydraulic measurements from 71 sites across Asia, Africa, Australia, the Americas and Europe. Samples span different soil textures and dry bulk densities. The records include water retention, unsaturated hydraulic conductivity, particle-size distribution, organic matter, depth, soil type and georeference. ZALF used the Extended Evaporation Method and HYPROP device to measure hydraulic properties from saturation towards wilting conditions. The named ZALF GeoNode resource page opened publicly; DataCite lists CSV and CC BY 4.0, with no fee indicated. Water and agricultural modellers could use the properties to calibrate soil-water flow and irrigation simulations across contrasting soils. These are measured samples from research projects, not a spatially exhaustive soil map. The exact sample distribution and field-to-file mapping were not checked by downloading the CSV. The public map view did not show a direct CSV link in its visible resource menu, so the file retrieval route remains uncertain. This resource is related to the site-specific soil hydrology data G4-0578 but covers many soils instead of one station. A full local duplicate scan found no catalogue identity match.
